brief: AI chip-debt SPVs are stampeding: Broadcom is arranging over $50bn for OpenAI's custom chips (talks with Apollo and Blackstone), Oracle is negotiating an off-balance-sheet vehicle with Apollo and Goldman to bridge chip costs against delayed cloud revenue, and SpaceX is seeking roughly $40bn after already issuing $65bn of debt since its June IPO (76% of IPO proceeds). Goldman's Privorotsky argues this borrowing, on top of hyperscalers' projected $500-800bn of debt issuance next year, is crowding out other borrowers from capital markets and keeping yields elevated: Q3 AI-ecosystem interest-rate-risk issuance ran about 25% above all Treasury issuance, and off-balance-sheet hyperscaler liabilities hit $3.8tn, up $700bn since June. The piece ties this to credit cracks: SpaceX's 5-year CDS hit a record 197bp, Oracle's bonds yield over 8% after the Project Jupiter force majeure, and USD CCC spreads closed near 998bp, the 99th percentile of the year, while IG spreads stayed flat at 80bp. Privorotsky frames the outcome as a fork: AI becomes self-financing via its own cash flow, or capital gets rationed and weaker credits break; the piece argues the second path is already being priced.
